newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler CFO says 1996 dividend possible.
newsitem.headline: Daimler CFO says 1996 dividend possible.

text.p: It is possible that German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG will pay a dividend to shareholders in 1996, Daimler's chief financial officer Manfred Gentz, said in a magazine interview on Wednesday.
"The way things lie at the moment we will report a good operating profit in 1996," Gentz said in an advance copy of an article due to appear in the Boerse Online magazine on Thursday.
While Gentz was unable to confirm whether or not a dividend would be paid on 1996 earnings he said: "The perspectives are not so bad."
In 1995 Daimler did not pay a dividend for the first time in over four decades after record losses of 5.7 billion marks.
In the first half of 1996, Daimler returned to the black with profits of 728 million marks.
Gentz said that group performance in the second half of 1996 would be even better than in the first half, provided nothing extraordinary happened over the coming months.
One of the main drivers behind the improved group performance was its Mercedes-Benz car division. Daimler's commercial vehicles unit also contributed to the strong performance.

Gentz said there was however "an earnings problem" in the group's European truck division. Its new Actros heavy trucks were cheaper to produce than their predecessors, but costs still needed to be cut at the production plants.
"In two years, at latest three years, our European truck unit will also be bringing in revenues," said Gentz.
Daimler to finalise restructuring plans Jan 23

The restructuring plan, part of the company's efforts to make individual units more profitable, has reportedly sparked wide-spread debate within Daimler, especially regarding the fate of Mercedes-Benz chief Helmut Werner.
Werner has opposed efforts to integrate the car and truck division more closely into the group structure, even threatening to resign, according to some reports.
